title: FDA Appendix G step 1: the within-reference variance, and which R is R1
subject: reference variance estimator

terms.Dij: Rij1 - Rij2, the difference between a subject's two observations on R, on the log scale
SUM_j Dij / n_i, the mean of Dij within sequence i
terms.n: SUM_i n_i, the total number of subjects used in the study
terms.m: the number of sequences used in the study
terms.Iij: Tij - (Rij1 + Rij2)/2 for the partial replicate; the mean of the test observations minus the mean of the reference observations for the fully replicate design

rule.degrees_of_freedom: n - m; the 2 in the denominator converts the variance of a difference into a variance and is NOT a degrees-of-freedom term

r1_r2_assignment.why_this_matters: R1 and R2 must come from the design, not from row order. FDA states the assignment as explicit SAS conditions on sequence and period, which is a directly checkable specification.
r1_r2_assignment.sas_partial_reference_1: if (seq=1 and per=2) or (seq=2 and per=1) or (seq=3 and per=1)   [seq 1=TRR, 2=RTR, 3=RRT]
r1_r2_assignment.sas_partial_reference_2: if (seq=1 and per=3) or (seq=2 and per=3) or (seq=3 and per=2)
r1_r2_assignment.sas_fully_reference_1: if (seq=1 and per=2) or (seq=2 and per=1)   [seq 1=TRTR, 2=RTRT]
r1_r2_assignment.sas_fully_reference_2: if (seq=1 and per=4) or (seq=2 and per=3)
r1_r2_assignment.engine_rule: reference periods in ascending period order; R1 is the earlier. Reproduces every row above.

sas_equivalence.partial: PROC GLM model dlat=seq, then s2wr = ms/2. The error mean square is SS/(n-m), so s2wr = SS/(2(n-m)) - the closed form.
sas_equivalence.fully: PROC MIXED model dlat=seq, then s2wr = estimate/2, taking the residual covariance parameter. The same quantity.
sas_equivalence.note: PROC GLM vs PROC MIXED distinguishes the treatment-contrast analysis (ilat), where a four-period design needs Satterthwaite degrees of freedom. It does not distinguish the sWR calculation.

history: Added after the guidance was obtained and read. The preceding release implemented only the partial-replicate estimator and had the fully-replicate one decline, inferring from 'PROC MIXED should be used for fully replicate (four-way) BE studies' that sWR required a mixed model. Appendix G gives the calculation once for both designs, distinguished only by m. The inference was wrong and the caution was misplaced.

source.section: Appendix G (highly variable drugs), step 1 and the SAS examples
source.verified_by: primary document, read at the cited section
source.limitation: The guidance states the algorithm and the SAS route but contains NO worked dataset - no input values and no published answer anywhere in the document. So this closes tier 1A and cannot close tier 1B, which needs numbers to reproduce. Obtaining this document was never going to close 1B; that requires a different source.

covers: The estimator's definition, its degrees of freedom, and the R1/R2 assignment. It asserts nothing about the RSABE criterion or the upper confidence bound, which are not implemented.
